title: Physics-Constrained Diffusion for Lightweight Composite Material Design
experiments_summary: The experiments use an in-house dataset of 3,400 carbon composite entries, where each entry describes proportions of carbon fiber, epoxy, and up to four fillers (CNTs, Graphene, Copper, Nickel) along with two target properties: Yield Strength (MPa) and Thermal Conductivity (W/mK). The proposed PCDiff model is compared against two baselines: a conditional VAE and TabDDPM. Four evaluation metrics are used: (1) Validity_reg, measuring the fraction of generated samples satisfying non-negativity and sum-to-one constraints, with one sample generated per training instance's property values; (2) Validity_fab, measuring the fraction of generated samples falling within a domain-expert-defined fabrication-feasible region, with fixed target property values of 3,500 MPa and 1.0 W/mK and 100 samples generated per model; (3) Density, assessing fidelity of generated samples; and (4) Coverage, assessing diversity of generated samples. The PCDiff model incorporates two physics-based regularization terms into the standard DDPM training objective—one penalizing negative component proportions and one penalizing deviation from a sum-to-one constraint—with weighting coefficients controlling the trade-off between data distribution fidelity and constraint satisfaction. A shallow MLP serves as the forward property predictor used during conditional generation.
